nodes.name: boost_9v
nodes.description: MT3608 boost converter generates the internal VCC_9V rail from the global USB_5V input for the NE5532 preamplifier stage only. EN should be configured for the intended always-on or controlled-enable policy using the provided EN pin. FB belongs to the output regulation network that will be implemented downstream. This module is the sole provider of VCC_9V and should not be used to power digital logic or the PAM8403.

nodes.name: power_3v3
nodes.description: AMS1117-3.3 LDO generates the internal VCC_3V3 rail from the global USB_5V input for the ATmega328P and MCP4725. This module is the sole provider of VCC_3V3 for the digital/control domain. Downstream wiring should keep the 3.3V distribution referenced to common GND while respecting the board-level analog/digital star-ground intent.

nodes.name: mcu_control
nodes.description: ATmega328P provides system control on VCC_3V3. It is the I2C bus master for the MCP4725 using the provided PC4/PC5 pins as the intended TWI interface, and it may optionally manage amplifier control policy through available GPIO if later needed. Both VCC and AVCC require VCC_3V3 supply distribution in downstream wiring; both GND pins return to common GND. AREF remains a local reference-related node for later schematic handling. This module owns the shared I2C master-side routing intent and should be kept in the digital branch of the star-ground topology.

nodes.name: dac_gain_control
nodes.description: MCP4725 is a single-channel I2C DAC powered from VCC_3V3. It receives commands from the MCU over the shared I2C bus and outputs one analog control voltage on VOUT. A0 must be tied in downstream wiring to select the intended I2C address. Because only one DAC channel is provided, it can implement only a shared stereo GAIN_CTRL or bias-control function, not independent left/right control. The DAC analog output should be routed toward the NE5532 control/bias network through a passive/interface network added later; no complete voltage-controlled gain circuit is required in this phase.

nodes.name: VOUT
nodes.description: DAC analog output, rail-to-rail (0 to VDD).

nodes.name: VDD
nodes.description: Supply voltage (2.7-5.5V), also serves as DAC reference.

nodes.name: SDA
nodes.description: I2C data, open-drain. Requires external pull-up on bus.

nodes.name: SCL
nodes.description: I2C clock, open-drain. Requires external pull-up on bus.

nodes.name: A0
nodes.description: I2C address bit. VSS=0x60, VDD=0x61. Must not float.

nodes.name: stereo_preamp
nodes.description: NE5532 dual op-amp implements the stereo preamplifier stage, with one amplifier channel for left and one for right signal path. It is powered from the generated VCC_9V rail and common GND using the provided VCC_P and VCC_N pins, implying single-supply operation referenced to ground unless downstream circuitry establishes another bias arrangement. The shared GAIN_CTRL analog input from the DAC feeds a passive or bias-control network that influences both channels according to the brief; this preserves control intent without requiring a complete voltage-controlled gain implementation. This module outputs PREAMP_L and PREAMP_R to the PAM8403 input stage and should be placed in the analog branch of the star-ground topology.

nodes.name: speaker_amplifier
nodes.description: PAM8403 is the stereo Class-D power amplifier powered directly from the global USB_5V rail via both VDD and PVDD pins. It receives analog left/right inputs from the NE5532 preamp and drives bridged stereo speaker outputs. MUTE and SHDN exist in the provided pin list and must be given a defined operating policy downstream; if no active control is used, they should be biased for normal playback. VREF is a local reference/bias-related node for downstream handling. The OUT_L_P/OUT_L_N and OUT_R_P/OUT_R_N pairs are bridged outputs and must connect only to the respective speaker terminals, not to GND. High-current output return routing should meet the common-ground star intent while keeping switching currents away from low-level analog and MCU areas.
